chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Musa, who said: 'It narrated to me Ali ibn Sulayman, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn Hakim, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:'
Feed the feverish the meat of Al-Qibaj (a type of pheasant), for it strengthens the two legs and repulses the fever with a repelling.

key_terms.الْقِبَاجِ: A type of bird (pheasant/partridge) mentioned in hadith

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended dietary treatment for fever in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) prescribes the meat of 'Al-Qibaj' (likely a pheasant or partridge) as a therapeutic remedy for fever, highlighting its dual benefit of strengthening the legs and expelling heat. This reflects the Shia tradition of integrating practical medicine with spiritual guidance, where specific foods are viewed as having inherent properties (*khawas*) that aid in healing. The emphasis on 'strengthening the legs' suggests a holistic approach to recovery, addressing both the systemic fever and the physical weakness often accompanying it.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Musa, from Ali Bin Suleyman, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muhammad Bin Hakeym, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 1st having said: ‘
Feed the feverish the meat of الْقِبَاجِ (a type of pheasant), for it strengthens the two legs and repulses the fever with a repelling’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn Musa who has said that narrated to me Ali ibn Sulayman from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Muhammad ibn Hakim who has said the following: “Abu al-Hassan, al-Awwal, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Feed one who is suffering from fever with the meat of al-Qabaj (a kind of partridge) because it strengthens the legs and dispels fever completely.’”
